## Glossary

**api-token-input**  
Class: reading a Kingdom API token only from stdin or KINGDOM_TOKEN; never argv, never stored.

**/api/v1/me/overview**  
Kingdom's user route listing owners, integrations and Signets the viewer can reach.

**described / revoked / unavailable**  
A held Signet's state as kcp status reports it from Kingdom.

**enrollment**  
Registering this machine's key on a Signet so it can present it.

**hold lock**  
signet's per-directory lock so concurrent logins and syncs never enroll over each other.

**holdPersonSignets / holdInstallationSignets**  
@inixiative/signet functions that enroll Signets under the hold lock.

**HOSTED_KINGDOM_URL**  
https://api.kingdom.inixiative.com, defaultKingdomUrl's final fallback.

**installation layout**  
@inixiative/signet's private files: <host>/installation-key.json and <host>/signet-<id>.json.

**kcp installation kind**  
The installation kind pairing needs; not yet in signet or Kingdom, so pairing refuses.

**KCP integration**  
The integration Kingdom creates for the approving owner; the owner grants it Signets.

**KCP_HOME**  
KCP's private directory (default ~/.kcp), one subdirectory per Kingdom host; resolved by kcpHome.

**Kingdom**  
The service that holds each integration's long-lived credential and runs Signet execute calls.

**Kingdom API token**  
A person's token for Kingdom's own API (login, map); never stored, never sent to an integration.

**kingdom-map**  
Class: kcp map and the /api/v1/me/overview read into owners and integrations.

**kingdom-settings**  
Class: which Kingdom URL a command uses and where KCP_HOME is.

**KINGDOM_TOKEN**  
Env var read only when --token env asks for it.

**KINGDOM_URL**  
Env var naming the Kingdom; after --url, before the last login's URL.

**login-session**  
Class: kcp login (pairing, --token, --signet), logout and status over signet's installation layout.

**owner**  
An organization, space, user or membership (OrganizationUser, SpaceUser) that owns integrations.

**pairing**  
Plain kcp login: this machine becomes an installation an owner approves (pairKcp).

**provider family**  
railway, github, vercel or infisical, from the family in Kingdom's provider catalog.

**requestSignet / awaitSignet**  
signet calls behind login --token --request: ask the owner for a Signet, then wait.

**secret-redaction**  
Class: removing secrets from text before it is printed (redactSecrets).

**Signet**  
An owner's grant on an integration's resources, held here as one credential file.

**Signet renewal credential**  
Secret inside a held Signet that redactSecrets strips from printed text.

**--token -|env**  
The only token sources: stdin or KINGDOM_TOKEN; any other value is refused.

## 1. What this Warden covers

How KCP signs a machine in to one Kingdom and keeps that session: which Kingdom and which local directory, the three logins plus logout and status, the rules for Kingdom API tokens and printed secrets, and the /api/v1/me/overview read behind kcp map.

## 2. The domain

kingdom-settings answers 'which Kingdom, and where on disk'. defaultKingdomUrl is the one to call: --url, then KINGDOM_URL, then the last login's Kingdom (savedKingdomUrl, written by saveKingdomUrl after a login), then the hosted https://api.kingdom.inixiative.com. kcpHome gives the KCP_HOME (default ~/.kcp) base every other function takes. Under it sits @inixiative/signet's installation layout: one directory per Kingdom host, a device key and one signet-<id>.json per Signet, private 0700/0600. KCP never writes those files itself.

login-session holds the logins and the session view. pairKcp is plain kcp login, browser pairing as a kcp installation. It refuses until signet and Kingdom declare the kcp installation kind, and points at --token and --signet instead. loginWithToken acts as an API token's person: it enrolls one Signet with --signet, enrolls the confirmed Signets with a prompt or --yes, or requests a new Signet with --request. loginWithSignet copies in a credential file or enrolls one Signet id. holdGrantedSignets syncs later grants for a paired installation. All enrollment runs under signet's per-directory hold lock. status gives the live view of the pairing and each held Signet. pairedInstallation reads only the local pairing record. logout deletes local state and prints what the owner must still revoke in Kingdom. The kcp bin reads a Kingdom API token only from --token - (stdin) or --token env (KINGDOM_TOKEN). The token never comes from argv, is never stored and never reaches an integration (api-token-input). Before any error is printed, redactSecrets removes Kingdom secrets, Signet renewal credentials and tokens from it (secret-redaction).

kingdom-map is kcp map. readOverview fetches /api/v1/me/overview with a user API token (not a Signet) and overviewSchema parses it. kingdomMap groups integrations under owners and formatMap renders that as text. enrollableSignets and signetIntegrationIds feed login --token, and integrationFamily names an integration's provider family. Not here: selector flags, providerFamilyOf for a binary name, routing, .foundry/kcp.json, operation parsers and runCommand (command-proxy); what KCP is, what is still pending, the kcp bin's dispatcher and bun run check (kcp-scope-and-cli).

### Class `login-session`: kcp login (browser pairing as a kcp installation, --token, --signet), logout, status over signet's installation layout: pairKcp, loginWithToken, loginWithSignet, holdGrantedSignets, hold lock, enrollment, supportedInstallationKind

**Job: get Signets onto this machine's key** (pairKcp vs loginWithToken vs loginWithSignet vs holdGrantedSignets) — README.md § Commands

*Said as:* "sign this machine in to Kingdom", "log in with my Kingdom API token", "I already have a Signet file", "pick up the Signets the owner just granted"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **pairKcp** | plain kcp login: pair as a kcp installation an owner approves | the kcp kind is not declared yet, or you hold a token or file (use loginWithToken or loginWithSignet) |
| **loginWithToken** | acting as an API token's person to enroll, confirm or request Signets | you have one Signet file or id (use loginWithSignet) |
| **loginWithSignet** | copying in a credential file or enrolling one Signet id | choosing among a person's Signets (use loginWithToken) |
| **holdGrantedSignets** | syncing later grants for an already paired installation | first enrollment by id or token (use loginWithSignet or loginWithToken) |

**Job: see or clear what this machine holds** (status vs pairedInstallation vs logout vs kingdomMap) — README.md § Commands

*Said as:* "what is this machine signed in with", "is this machine paired already", "sign out and delete the local keys", "show everything I could reach in Kingdom"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **status** | live view of the pairing and each held Signet as Kingdom describes it | only the local pairing record is needed (use pairedInstallation) |
| **pairedInstallation** | checking locally whether this KCP is paired | you need each Signet's live state (use status) |
| **logout** | withdrawing pairing and deleting this machine's key and Signets for one Kingdom | revoking in Kingdom, which stays with the owner |
| **kingdomMap (kingdom-session)** | what Kingdom offers: every reachable owner and integration | only what is held here (use status) |

**Job: choose the login command a person runs** (kcp login vs --token vs --token --request vs --signet) — README.md § Commands

*Said as:* "which login command should the user run", "request access to an integration from the owner", "log in on a headless machine without a browser"

| Member | Use when | Not when (use instead) |
|---|---|---|
| **kcp login** | browser pairing as an installation | the kcp kind is not declared yet (use kcp login --token or --signet) |
| **kcp login --token** | you have a Kingdom API token and Signets already exist | no Signet is granted yet (use kcp login --token --request) |
| **kcp login --token --request** | asking the owner for a Signet on -i's resources and waiting | a Signet already exists (use kcp login --token) |
| **kcp login --signet** | you hold a Signet file or id | you need to discover Signets (use kcp login --token) |

#### Commands

```
kcp login [--url URL] [--name NAME] [--organization SLUG|ID] [--no-open]
kcp login --token -|env [--signet SIGNET_ID | --yes] [--url URL]
kcp login --token -|env --request -i INTEGRATION_ID --operation OP [--operation OP…]
kcp login --signet FILE|SIGNET_ID [--token -|env] [--url URL]
kcp logout [--url URL]
kcp status [--url URL]
kcp map [--json] --token -|env [--url URL]

kcp [selectors] <railway|gh|vercel|infisical> <args…>
```

Every login ends the same way: a device key plus one credential file per Signet, private (0700 directory, 0600 files) under `KCP_HOME` (default `~/.kcp`), one directory per Kingdom host. The layout is `@inixiative/signet`'s installation layout (`<host>/installation-key.json`, `<host>/signet-<id>.json`), so a Foundry or Archive reads it the same way.

- **`kcp login`** pairs this machine as a KCP installation (`pairInstallation`). A person approves it in Kingdom as an owner, and Kingdom creates that owner's KCP integration. The owner then grants the integration Signets on Railway, GitHub and the rest; KCP enrolls each grant (`holdInstallationSignets`) at login, on `status` and before each command.
- **`kcp login --token`** acts as the person a Kingdom API token belongs to. With `--signet <id>` it enrolls this key on that one Signet. Without, it lists the Signets issued to the person, or to one of their memberships (OrganizationUser, SpaceUser), on integrations whose provider family KCP serves (by the `family` in Kingdom's provider catalog) and not held here yet, and enrolls them only once confirmed: a prompt when a person can answer, `--yes` otherwise. Enrollment goes through `@inixiative/signet`'s `holdPersonSignets`, under the same per-directory hold lock as installation syncs, so two logins (or a login and a sync) never enroll over each other. With `--request -i … --operation …` it asks for a Signet on that integration's resources instead (`requestSignet`) and waits for the owner (`awaitSignet`).
- **The token never goes on the command line.** `--token -` reads it from stdin; `--token env` reads `KINGDOM_TOKEN`, which is read only when `--token env` asks for it. Any other value is refused, because an argument lands in shell history and the process list. The token is used for the call and never stored. A Kingdom API token is for Kingdom's own API (`login`, `map`); it never reaches an integration.
- **`kcp login --signet <file>`** copies an existing credential file in; its key stays where it is. **`--signet <id>`** enrolls that Signet through the paired installation (`enrollInstallationSignet`), or as its person with `--token`.
- **`kcp logout`** withdraws an open pairing and deletes this machine's key and Signets for that Kingdom. Revoking stays with Kingdom, so it prints the Signet ids (and the KCP integration, if paired) the owner should revoke there. A withdrawal Kingdom refused is reported, and the command exits 1.
- **`kcp status`** shows the pairing and each held Signet as Kingdom describes it now (`described`, `revoked` or `unavailable`), with its integration, provider and owner.
- **`kcp map`** prints every owner you can reach and their integrations, with ids to pass to `-i`, and marks the ones you manage and the Signets this machine holds. `--json` prints the structure.

The Kingdom is `--url`, else `KINGDOM_URL`, else the one the last login used, else `https://api.kingdom.inixiative.com`.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#built-and-pending -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Built and pending (in "@inixiative/kcp")

#### Built and pending

Built (v0): the three logins, `logout`, `status`, `map`, selector parsing, routing, `.foundry/kcp.json`, the parser registry and the execute path behind it.

Waiting on Kingdom and `@inixiative/signet`:

- **The `kcp` installation kind.** Browser pairing needs `kcp` in signet's `installationKindSchema`, Kingdom's `InstallationKind` and `Provider` enums, and its catalog. None of the existing kinds fits: pairing as `foundry` creates a Foundry integration with a `threads` resource, `oracle` would show as an Oracle, and `archive` requires a `sourceId`. Until then `kcp login` says so and points to `--token` and `--signet`; once signet declares the kind, it works with no KCP change.
- **CLI operations** (§9, §11 step 1): resource kinds and operation input schemas for Railway, GitHub, Vercel and Infisical in signet's contracts, then one parser each here.
- **The runner** and its delivery value (§6), and **output streaming** over the Signet socket. Until then `execute` returns the result whole.
- **`/me/overview` through a Signet.** The overview is a user route (JWT or API token), so `kcp map` needs `--token`. Routing doesn't: it reads the held Signets through `access/describe`.
- **`credential.release`** for the git credential helper and local commands (§4), then `kcp shims install` and `kcp hook claude|codex`. Until the helper exists, `kcp git …` is refused.
- **Membership recipients in Kingdom.** `login --token` offers Signets issued to the person's OrganizationUser and SpaceUser memberships (matched by the recipient's user id), but Kingdom's `SignetRecipientModel` is `User | Integration` today and `/me/overview` lists only those, so none arrive yet.
